Md Momztaz Uddin Fakir, Advocate—For the Petitioners. 

None appears—For the Opposite-Parties.
parties:
Ditandra Bikash Bonik and others -------- Petitioners
Vs.
Hamida Begum and others ---------- Opposite-Parties
full_judgment:
This rule has been issued calling upon the opposite parties Nos.1-10 to show cause as to why the judgment dated 18th August, 1997 of the learned Additional District Judge, Hobiganj in Title Appeal No. 86 of 1985 should not be set aside.

2. Girindra Chandra Bonik, the predecessor of the present petitioners as plaintiffs instituted Title Suit No. 55 of 1981 before the Subordinate Judge, Hobiganj impleading the predecessor of the present opposite parties Nos. 1-9 and other opposite parties as defendants under Order XXI, rule 103 of the Code of Civil Procedure for establishment of right and possession in the suit premises.

3. The case of the predecessor of the petitioner is that late Girindra Chandra Bonik entered into an agreement with late Nandalal Roy for purchase of the suit property for a consideration of Taka 6000. Pursuant thereto the said Nandalal Roy on receipt of a part consideration executed a kabala in favour of the opposite party No. 11 for and on behalf of the said Girindra Chandra Bonik with an assurance that he would register the kabala on receipt of the income tax clearance certificate and the balance of the purchase price from the said Girindra Chandra Bonik. The said Nandalal Roy did not take steps for obtaining income tax clearance certificate on receipt of the balance of the consideration of sale price. As such the said Girindra Chandra Banik instituted Title Suit No. 13 of 1963 for Specific performance of contract against the said Nandalal Roy, who filed a written statement in the said suit and upon an application being filed by said Girindra Chandra Banik a temporary injunction was issued against the said Nandalal Roy restraining him from transferring the suit property. Nandalal Roy was examined on commission on 12th June, 1966 and in cross-examination he admitted the execution of the kabala as aforesaid. Thereafter, the said Nandalal Roy did not contest the suit. Girindra Chandra Banik obtained permission under the disturbed persons rehabilitation Ordinance and deposited in Court the said permission and the balance consideration money. Thereafter the suit was taken up for hearing but as none appeared on behalf of the said Nandalal Roy, the Court passed an ex parte decree on 20 July, 1966 in favour of the said Girindra Chandra Banik. Thereafter, the said Nandalal Roy filed an application under Order IX, rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure for restoration of the suit in Miscellaneous Case No. 16 of 1966; during the pendency of the said Miscellaneous Case Nandalal Roy died on 12th November, 1966. The said Miscellaneous Case was dismissed for non prosecution. The further case of the petitioners is that in execution of the said decree, the said Girindra Chandra Banik obtained a kabala executed by the only son and heir of the said Nandalal Roy, and obtained delivery of possession through Court on 30th April, 1969 evicting the men of late Mobashwar Ali who were in possession of the suit property. On the same day the evicted persons came in a body and trespassed into the suit property assaulting the said Girindra Chandra Banik and his wife opposite party No.11 and on receipt of information, the police appeared in the scene and drove out the trespassers and restored the possession to the said Girindra Chandra Banik who remained in possession and after his death, the petitioners and opposite party No. 11 and 12 are still in possession of the suit property. The further case of the petitioners is that the said Mobashwar Ali instituted Miscellaneous Case No.71 of 1969 under Order XXI, rule 101 of the Code of Civil Procedure which though contested by the said Girindra Chandra Banik, was allowed on 9th July, 1980 directing restoration of possession to him. Against the said order Girindra Chandra Banik commenced a proceeding against the said Mobashwar Ali and the opposite party No. 10 claiming a right to the suit property on the basis of the aforesaid decree, consequent kabala and delivery of possession through Court which was registered as Title Suit No. 55 of 1981 in the Court of the Subordinate Judge, Habiganj.

4. Mobashwar AU, the predecessor of opposite party Nos. 1-9 contested the suit by filing written statement contending inter alia that the aforesaid Nandalal Roy and his younger brother Jogendra Lal Roy, father of the opposite party No. 10 were members of a Joint Hindu family and Nandalal Roy purchased the suit land with the joint family fund, and, as such, he owned it in equal shares. There was an amicable partition between the brothers by an unregistered deed of partition dated 1st October, 1960 wherein the said Jogendra Lal Roy got the suit property in his share. The said Jogendra Lal Roy thereafter instituted partition suit No.28 of 1968 which was decreed on the basis of the said deed of partition dated 1st October, 1960. The said Jogendra Lai Roy thereafter executed a kabala in favour of the said Mobashwar Ali whose man came in possession of the suit property and were evicted in course of delivery of possession through Court of the suit property on 30th April, 1969 in execution of the alleged decree in Title Suit No. 13 of 1963. In the foregoing situation the said Girindra Chandra Bonik did not acquire any right, title and interest in the suit property.

5. By his judgment dated 3st March, 1985, the learned Subordinate Judge on consideration of documentary and oral evidence adduced by the parties, decreed the suit in favour of the said Girindra Chandra Bonik on the finding that the said Mobashwar Ali failed to prove his case.

6. The appellate Court reversed the decision and finding of the trial Court by judgment and decree dated 18.08.1997 against which the instant rule.

7. Mr. Momtaz Uddin Fakir learned advocate, appearing for the petitioners submits that Order 21 Rule 103 of the Code of Civil Procedure is not appealable and this vital point has been raised before the appellate Court but the appellate Court without adverting and considering that vital point allowed the appeal which caused serious miscarriage of justice. He next submits that learned Additional District Judge committed error in reversing the decision of the Court of 1st instance without reversing the findings recorded by it who arrived at a decision on true and proper consideration of the oral and documentary evidence. He next submits that the appellate Court failed to consider that Nandalal Roy being purchaser of the suit land by sale deed dated 8th Jaistho 1360 BS by his own money and benefit entered into agreement with the plaintiff for sale on 4-7-1962 but subsequently Nandalal resiled from his agreement and refused to execute and register deed of sale for which the plaintiff by filing Title Suit No. 13 of 1963 got decree in his favour which has been duly executed through execution case. The plea of suit property being jointly owned by Nandalal Roy and Jogendra Lal Roy have not been proved by evidence but the appellate Court failed to advert that vital aspect of the case and erroneously allowed the appeal which caused failure of justice.

8. Having gone through the pleadings, exhibits and other documents it appears that Girindra Chandra Bonik, the predecessor of the present petitioners instituted Title Suit No. 13 of 1963 before the first Court of Subordinate Judge, Sylhet for specific performance of contract wherein Nanda Lal Roy made appearance, contested the suit by filing written statement and subsequently deposed on commission on 16-6-1966 admitting transfer of suit land in favor of the plaintiff of the suit. As he failed to appear subsequently, the suit was decreed exparte and for setting aside the said exparte decree Nandalal Roy filed Miscellaneous Case No. 16 of 1966. On the death of Nandalal Roy his daughter Sushama Bala Roy claiming herself as heir of late Nanda Lal made prayer of substituting herself in the said miscellaneous case but subsequently it is detected that Nanda Lal Roy has a son namely Nagendra

Lal Roy and, as such, application for substitution of Sushama Bala Roy was rejected and consequent civil revision being Civil Revision No. 103 of 1968 filed before the High Court Division was also rejected. Thereafter Girindra Chandra Bonik filed Execution Case No. 10 of 1967 and got a deed of sale executed and registered and by filing title Execution Case No.8 of 1969 got delivery of possession on 30-4-1969.

9. It further appears that Jogendra Lal Roy, the brother of Nanda Lal Roy filed Partition Suit No. 28 of 1968 claiming joint family property with Nanda Lal Roy and the said partition suit was decreed exparte on 26-4-1968. Thereafter defendant No.1 by filing Miscellaneous Case No. 71 of 1969 under Order XXI, rules 101 of the Code of Civil Procedure prayed for restoration of possession purportedly claiming the suit land by virtue of baina patra having executed by Jogendra Lal Roy dated 7-12-1963 and after hearing the said case was allowed ordering restoration of possession. Challenging the said judgment and order, the petitioners filed Title Suit No.51 of 1981 before the Subordinate Judge, Habiganj under Order XXI, rules 103 of the Code of Civil Procedure.

10. The trial Court in his judgment held that there is no convincing evidence that Nanda Lal Roy and Jogendra Lal jointly held and possessed the suit land. The trial court with reference to DW 4 Abul Hossain, DW 5 Chunu Mia and DW 10 Shaheb Mia held that Nanda Lal resided in the suit premises till his death and defendant No.1failed to prove that on the basis of baina patra he went to the possession of the suit land on 7-12-1963. The trial court with reference to DW 1 Azizul Haque found that he himself and other persons resided in the suit land time to time. The Court also discussed the evidence of DWs 5, 6, 8, 9, 10 and 11 and held that there are anomalies in their deposition regarding possession of the suit land and that defendant No. 1 did not enter into the suit land by virtue of the baina patra dated 7-12-1963, rather the men of defendant No.1 came to the suit land after the death of Nanda Lal Roy. The trial Court also disbelieved the baina patra as claimed by defendant No. 1 and also found that Jogendra Lal Roy never claimed the suit land during the lifetime of Nanda Lal Roy. The trial Court also held that the plaintiff after getting decree in a suit for specific performance of contract got kabala through court and also obtained possession by filing execution case. The Court found that Jogendra Lal Roy filed Title Suit No. 28 of 1968 in the third Court of Munsif, Habigonj and obtained preliminary decree on 26-4-1968 impleading Nanda Lal's son Nagendra Lal Roy as defendant No.1 and Nanda Lal's daughter as defendant No. 2 although the address of defendant No.1 was shown at Habigonj town but it is claimed that his whereabouts was not known and Sushama Bala was no legal heir of Nanda Lal Roy and, as such, the decree has been obtained by practising fraud and for unknown reason Sushama Bala did not contest the suit. The trial Court by elaborate discussion also held that there is no trace that Jogendra Lal Roy and Nanda Lal Roy jointly held and possessed the suit land as member of joint family and, as such, alleged purported unregistered Batwaranama and other documents shown by defendant No.1 are nothing but collusive and created papers and accordingly the trial Court decreed the suit in favour of the plaintiff upholding plaintiff's possession.

11. Before the Appellate Court contention was raised on behalf of the petitioner-respondent that an order passed in the proceeding under rule 103 of Order XXI of the Code of Civil Procedure is conclusive and no appeal is maintainable against such order but the appellate Court disregarding the legal provision and established principle held that since it is a regular suit and decree is drawn thereon as such appeal is maintainable. Such view is patently illegal and not sustainable. For proper appreciation, rule 103 of Order XXI is reproduced below:

"Any party not being a judgment-debtor against whom an order is made under rule 98. rule 99 or rule 101 may institute a suit to establish the right which he claims to the present possession of the property; but, subject to the result of such suit (if any), the order shall be conclusive."

12. In the case of Nirmal Chandra Choudhury vs Nikunja Behari Biswas 6 DLR 333 it is held that:

"Under what authority, with due respect to the learned Judges in those cases, they came to this conclusion it is difficult for me to ascertain. Section 115 does not prevent any revision on the ground that there is another remedy. Rule 103 contains the words "subject to the result of such suit, (if any)" the order passed under Rules 98, 99 and 101 will be conclusive. The word 'conclusive' means no appeal lies but it does not mean that High Court cannot revise the order of the Court passed under Rules 98, 99 and 101 of the Code of Civil Procedure."

<u>13. Apart from this, right to prefer appeal is statutory right but in the instant matter rule 103 of Order XXI of the Code of Civil Procedure mandates that order passed under the said section will be final meaning hereby that there is no scope of appeal which is clearly reiterated in 6 DLR 333. Besides jurisdiction cuts the root of the matter and if the Court got no jurisdiction everything shall fall through. In the case of Managing Director, Rupali Bank limited vs Tafazal Hossain 44 DLR (AD) 260 it is held that:</u>

"Jurisdiction of a Court goes to the very root of a matter brought before it, and if the Court got no jurisdiction, everything shall fall through. We are surprised to find that the learned Single Judge in this case held that the Court's jurisdiction is a mere technicality and that it is the merit of a case that matters. The Court which got no jurisdiction over a matter shall not go into the merit of the matter. The view expressed by the learned Single Judge regarding jurisdiction is grievously erroneous. Similarly, the other view of the learned Single Judge is that in the present position of section 115 CPC, the question of `jurisdiction' is replaced by 'error of law' is equally faulty. The assistant Judge having no jurisdiction over the matter the decree passed in the suit is void."

14. So it is crystal clear that the opposite party committed error in preferring appeal against the impugned judgment and decree passed by the Trial Court and, as such, judgment passed in such appeal is not sustainable in the eye of law. Consequently, the judgment and decree passed by the trial Court remained unassailed.

15. The appellate Court also failed to consider that Girindra Chandra Bonik by filing Title Suit No. 13 of 1963 before the Subordinate Judge, Sylhet got a decree for specific performance of contract by virtue of baina patra dated 7-12-1963 which has not been denied by Nanda Lal Roy and by virtue of the said decree he got kabala and delivery of possession in the suit land by evicting the daughter of Nanda Lal and the other occupants of the suit land and since then the heirs of said Girindra Chandra Bonik i.e. the present petitioners are still in possession therein.

16. The appellate Court relied on the judgment and decree obtained by Jogendra Lal Roy in Title suit No.28 of 1968 whereby Jogendra Lal Roy got an exparte decree on 26-4-1968 for partition regarding the suit land and held that by said deed of partition Jogendra Lal Roy got a preliminary decree but appellate Court failed to consider that by virtue of a judgment and decree passed in a suit for specific performance of contract as mentioned above the suit land has been devolved upon the predecessor of the present petitioners who is succeeded by the present petitioners and admittedly they are in possession. The trial Court clearly held that the judgment and decree dated 26-4-1968 passed in Title Suit No. 28 of 1968 is outcome of fraud and forgery as it has been obtained in collusion with the daughter of Nanda Lai Roy without service of summons upon the son of Nanda Lal Roy namely Nogendra Lal Roy who is the actual successor-in-interest of Nanda Lal Roy and, as such, the opposite parties got no title or interest over the suit land but those vital facts also has not been controverted by the appellate Court who erroneously reversed the findings of the trial Court.

17. In the above factual scenarios it is clear that the judgment and decree passed by the appellate Court is not sustainable as per law. In fact the judgment and decree of the appellate Court is non-est in the eye of law and consequently the judgment and decree passed by the Court of first instance stands as an unassailed one.

18. In the above context, I find merit in the Rule and accordingly the Rule is made absolute without any order as to cost.

19. The order of status-quo granted at the time of issuance of the rule is hereby re-called and vacated.

Let a copy of the judgment along with the Lower Court record be sent to the concerned Court.

End.
